QUIC client idle-connection test that opens and tracks many connections.

# Purpose
This C file implements a QUIC client test program that opens and maintains many client connections to a remote IPv4 endpoint. It sets up QUIC connection callbacks, creates a QUIC instance in an anonymous workspace, configures a UDP socket for network I/O, and then enters an infinite service loop that drives QUIC processing and UDP socket processing. The program also creates new connections until it reaches the requested connection count, and it tracks connection state in the global `g_conn_meta` table with the counters `g_dead`, `g_init`, and `g_active`.

The [`main`](<#main>) function parses command-line options and environment settings for the source IP, destination IP, destination port, number of connections, workspace size, page size, and NUMA placement. It then initializes the QUIC client configuration, installs a test signer for TLS, validates the IP address inputs, and starts the client loop through [`run_quic_client`](<#run_quic_client>). The file uses the QUIC public API and test helper interfaces, so it acts as an executable test and load-generation tool rather than a reusable library.
